Grape___Black_rot.Environment: Warm temperatures (20–30°C), frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Grape___Black_rot.Spread: Fungal spores spread through rain splash, wind and infected plant debris.
Grape___Black_rot.Description: Black Rot is one of the most damaging fungal diseases of grapevines. It affects leaves, shoots and berries, causing severe yield losses if not managed.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small tan circular spots appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Black fruiting bodies develop in lesions and berries begin to shrivel.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Berries become hard black mummies and leaves dry prematurely.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms typically develop within 10–21 days after infection.

Symptoms: Brown leaf spots with black dots
Treatment: Apply fungicides during the growing season.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Scientific_Name: Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium minimum and Fomitiporia mediterranea
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Environment: Warm climates with stressed vines and pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Spread: Fungal spores enter through pruning wounds and infected wood.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Description: Esca is a complex trunk disease that damages the vascular system of grapevines. It weakens vines over several years and significantly reduces vineyard productivity.

Age_Cycle.Early: Interveinal yellow or reddish discoloration appears on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Wood decay progresses and berries develop dark spots.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Sudden vine collapse (apoplexy) may occur during hot weather.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease develops over several growing seasons.

Treatment: Protect pruning wounds with wound sealants.
Recommended_Chemicals: No fully curative chemical treatment available
Recommended_Actions: Protect pruning wounds immediately after pruning.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Environment: Warm temperatures (22–30°C), high humidity and prolonged periods of leaf wetness.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Spread: Fungal spores spread through wind, rain splash and infected plant debris.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Description: Leaf Blight is a fungal disease that primarily attacks grape leaves. Severe infection causes premature defoliation, reducing photosynthesis, fruit quality and vine vigor.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small brown spots develop on older leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge with gray centers and dark margins.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves dry, curl and fall prematurely.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms generally develop within 10–15 days after infection.

Recommended_Actions: Apply fungicides at the first sign of disease.

Grape___healthy.Environment: Well-drained fertile soil, full sunlight, balanced irrigation and good vineyard management.
Grape___healthy.Description: The uploaded grape leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease, pest infestation or nutrient deficiency. The vine appears healthy and capable of normal vegetative growth and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Moderate: Normal vine growth and canopy development.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth throughout the growing season.

Organic_Treatment: Apply balanced organic fertilizers when necessary.
